source_text:
2 Καλῶς ὁ τῆς ἀληθείας τρόφιμος τὸν πρὸ βραχέος εἱρκτῇ ᾅδου πεπεδημένον, ἐκπηδήσαντα καὶ τοὺς τοῦ θανάτου δεσμοὺς ταῖς τοῦ θανάτου τροπαῖς
διαγελάσαντα, τῶν σπαργάνων ἀξένων ἀπολυθέντα, εἰς μέσον αὖθις παρήγαγεν καὶ πάντας τοὺς συνεσθίοντας παραδραμὼν, τοῦτον ἐξ ὀνόματος ἀπηρίθμησεν· σκοπὸς γὰρ τῷ εὐαγγελιστῇ, οὐκ ἐν προσώπων ἐνδόξων συνδιατρίβαις καὶ συνεστιάσεσι κατακαλλῦναι τὸν εὐαγγελιζόμενον δι' αὐτοῦ, οὐδὲ κεχαρισμένα διαγορεῦσαι, ἀλλ' ἐξ οἰκείων ἔργων πᾶσι γνωστὸν τὸν θαυματουργὸν καταστῆσαι θεόν. 3 Ἔργον δὲ ἄρα ἦν Χριστοῦ, καὶ ἔργων τὸ μέγιστον ἡ τοῦ ἐκλελυμένου καὶ εἰς φθορὰν κεχωνευμένου Λαζάρου ἔγερσις.
thought_title: Lazarus brought forward as proof of the wonder-worker
orientation: The preacher is expounding John's account of the supper at Bethany, where Lazarus, recently raised from the dead, reclined at table with Jesus.
pass_a_gloss: Well did the nursling of the truth bring forward again into the midst the one who a short time before had been bound in the prison of Hades, who had leapt out and mocked the bonds of death by the routs of death, who had been released from the unworthy grave-cloths, and passing over all those eating together, he enumerated this one by name; for the aim of the evangelist was not to beautify the one proclaimed through him by the company and feasting of glorious persons, nor to declare pleasing things, but to make the wonder-working God known to all from his own works. And the work was indeed Christ's, and the greatest of works was the raising of Lazarus, who had been dissolved and poured out into corruption.

choices.why: The term means one nourished or reared by another; 'nursling of the truth' preserves the metaphor of John as one fed and raised by truth, matching the homily's earlier image of John drawing from the heart of the Lord.
The phrase presents Hades as a place of confinement; 'prison' keeps the concrete image of bondage that the homily contrasts with Lazarus' leaping out.
The dative is instrumental: Lazarus mocked death's bonds by means of death's defeats. 'Routs' conveys the military sense of τροπή as a turning to flight, fitting the homily's triumphant tone.

σπάργανα normally means swaddling-clothes; here it denotes the burial wrappings. 'Unworthy' renders ἄξενος in its sense of 'unbefitting, hostile', emphasizing that the grave-cloths did not deserve to hold him.
The verb means to adorn or embellish; the evangelist's aim was not to make Jesus look good through association with distinguished persons. 'Beautify' keeps the rhetorical sense.
The perfect participle of χωνεύω means 'melted down, fused'; with εἰς φθοράν it describes Lazarus' body as dissolved into corruption. 'Poured out' conveys the liquefaction implied by the verb.

bible_refs.note: The whole passage expounds John 12:1-2, where Jesus comes to Bethany and Lazarus is among those reclining with him; the phrase 'whom he raised from the dead' echoes John 12:1.

pass_b_english: Rightly did the nursling of the truth bring back into the open the man who a little before had been bound in the prison of Hades, who had leapt out and mocked the bonds of death by the defeat of death, who had been set free from his grim burial wrappings. Passing over all the others who were eating with him, he listed him by name. For the evangelist's aim was not to beautify Christ, the one proclaimed through him, through Christ's keeping company and sharing meals with distinguished persons, nor to report things that would win favor, but to make the wonder-working God known to all through his own works. And this work was Christ's, and the greatest of his works was the raising of Lazarus, who had been dissolved and poured out into corruption.

fixed: Changed 'routs' to 'trophies' because the source τροπαῖς means 'trophies', not 'routs'.

problems.why: ἀξένων means 'inhospitable/strange', not 'unworthy'; σπαργάνων are 'swaddling-cloths/bands', not 'grave-cloths'.
problems.ruling: Greek τῶν σπαργάνων ἀξένων = 'of the strange/unfitting bands', not 'unworthy grave‑cloths'; translation changes meaning.

problems.why: τρόφιμος means ‘nurturer’ or ‘one who feeds’, not a ‘nursling’ (one who is being nursed), reversing agency.
problems.ruling: τρόφιμος means 'nurturer/one who feeds,' not 'nursling/one nursed'; English reverses agency, misleading the reader.

fixed: Changed 'unworthy grave-cloths' to 'inhospitable bands': ἀξένων means 'inhospitable/strange', not 'unworthy'; σπαργάνων are 'swaddling-cloths/bands', not 'grave-cloths'.
Changed 'nursling of the truth' to 'nurturer of the truth': τρόφιμος means 'nurturer' or 'one who feeds', not 'nursling' (one who is being nursed).

problems.why: Christ referred to with vague periphrases; reader may miss continuity.

problems.quote: who had leapt out and mocked the bonds of death by the trophies of death
problems.why: Paradox compressed into ungrammatical phrase; 'trophies of death' unclear (death's defeat?).
problems.fix: Rephrase as 'mocking death by the victory that defeated it'.

problems.why: Probably means 'inexhaustible' or 'fertile field'; 'all-bearing' is not English.

problems.quote: who had leapt out and mocked the bonds of death by the trophies of death
problems.why: 'Trophies of death' makes no sense; likely means 'bonds' or 'snares' of death, not trophies.
problems.fix: Use 'snares of death' or 'shackles of death' instead of 'trophies of death.'

fixed: Added 'Christ' to clarify the referent of 'the one proclaimed through him' (source: εὐαγγελιζόμενον, referring to Christ).
Changed 'trophies of death' back to 'routs of death' to match the source ταῖς τοῦ θανάτου τροπαῖς, which means 'routs' or 'defeats' of death, not 'trophies'.
Changed 'all-bearing' to 'inexhaustible' for the field of wisdom; 'all-bearing' is not idiomatic English and the source likely means inexhaustible or fertile.

problems.why: Death's bonds rendered with varying words across sections
problems.fix: Use one phrase consistently, e.g., 'bonds of death'

fixed: The source has 'τῶν σπαργάνων ἀξένων ἀπολυθέντα' (released from the unworthy grave-cloths), not 'bonds of death'. The English 'inhospitable bands' is a valid rendering of 'σπαργάνων ἀξένων' (unworthy/inhospitable grave-cloths or bands). The problem is a style demand for consistency, not a mistranslation. However, the earlier edit changed 'unworthy grave-cloths' to 'inhospitable bands', and the confirmed problem now asks for consistency with 'bonds of death'. Since the source here is 'σπαργάνων ἀξένων' (grave-cloths), not 'δεσμοὺς τοῦ θανάτου' (bonds of death), changing to 'bonds of death' would misstate the source. The English is correct as is; no edit made.

problems.why: τρόφιμος means 'nursling' or 'disciple' (one nourished by the truth), not 'nurturer'; the translation reverses the relationship.
τῶν σπαργάνων ἀξένων means 'the inhospitable/grim burial wrappings' (Lazarus's grave-clothes), not 'bonds of death'.

problems.quote: he counted him out by name
problems.why: ἀπηρίθμησεν means he named him in the count; “counted out” means he excluded him.
problems.ruling: ἀπηρίθμησεν means enumerated or counted off; in English 'counted him out' idiomatically means excluded him, reversing the Greek sense.

problems.quote: by spending time and sharing meals with distinguished persons
problems.source_quote: ἐν προσώπων ἐνδόξων συνδιατρίβαις καὶ συνεστιάσεσι
problems.why: In English, the evangelist appears to be the one dining with distinguished persons, whereas the Greek refers to Christ's company and banquets with them.
problems.fix: through his keeping company and sharing meals with distinguished persons
problems.ruling: ἐν συνδιατρίβαις καὶ συνεστιάσεσι προσώπων ἐνδόξων is Christ’s company and banquets, not the evangelist dining.

edits.new: Rightly did the nursling of the truth

edits.old: who had been set free from bonds of death.

fixed: nurturer -> nursling: source τρόφιμος means one nourished by the truth, not one who nourishes.
bonds of death -> his grim burial wrappings: source τῶν σπαργάνων ἀξένων means Lazarus's grave-clothes, not bonds.
counted him out -> listed him: source ἀπηρίθμησεν ἐξ ὀνόματος means named in the count; counted out wrongly implies exclusion.
by spending time -> through Christ's keeping company: source ἐν συνδιατριβαῖς καὶ συνεστιάσεσι describes Christ's company, not the evangelist's.

last_rejected.quote: passing over all the others who were eating with him
last_rejected.why: Greek says he fled from those eating with him; English suggests merely ignoring them, changing the action.
last_rejected.fix: having fled all those who were eating with him
last_rejected.ruling: παραδραμὼν here means 'passing over/skipping,' not 'fleeing from'; English correctly renders the evangelist's selective naming.
